title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. In 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}', Y is the compactified moduli multiplicity (an orbifold or stack, Deligne–Mumford type) and D' is a boundary divisor, or a component or stratum of the boundary divisor Θ. D'* is the open stratum. N_{D',Y} is the normal bundle of D' in Y. P_{D'*} is the deleted (punctured) normal bundle over D'*, so (N minus its zero section) restricted to D'*. V_{D',Y} is a tubular neighbourhood. V^*_{D',Y} is the punctured tubular neighbourhood, i.e. V minus Θ.

Previous page. Grothendieck asks for an embedding (240) V_{D',Y} ↪ N_{D',Y}. It should restrict to the zero section on D' and induce the identity on normal bundles along the zero section, i.e. a differentiable tubular-neighbourhood map. He notes this exists for ordinary paracompact analytic spaces but can fail for multiplicities. His counterexample is Z acting on C^2 by the transvection (1 1; 0 1), with D' = (C^1, Z) and Y = (C^2, Z). The equivariant extension 0 → T_{D'} → T_Y|_{D'} → N → 0 is a non-split unipotent Z-module extension, so it is not the one coming from the zero section of a vector bundle.

This page. When such an embedding exists, it is a homotopy equivalence and so induces an equivalence on π_1. 'Mais [là] le bât blesse': in general one does not get this without assuming restrictive genericity hypotheses.

He then sketches a square of fundamental groupoids:
- top arrow: π_1^ouv P_{D'*} → π_1^rev V_{D',Y};
- vertical isomorphism: π_1^ouv P_{D'*} ≅ π_1^rev P_{D'*};
- an NB about π_1^ouv V.
Here π_1^ouv is the groupoid defined by points and paths ('points et arcs'), and π_1^rev the one defined through (1-connected) coverings. For multiplicities these are a priori different, as with orbifold or stack fundamental groupoids.

Marginal note. The composite V^*_{D'*} ↪ V^*_{D'} → P_{D'*} induces an equivalence on π_1. This follows from the equivalence between π_1 of non-singular loci and of their coverings, i.e. removing higher-codimension strata does not change the relevant π_1.

Main text. Choosing the embeddings (240) compatibly with the divisor Θ, the inverse image of P_{D'*} (an open subset of N_{D',Y}) is exactly V^*_{D',Y}. One therefore gets a retraction-type morphism (241) V^*_{D',Y} → P_{D'*}, hence (242) π_1 V^*_{D',Y} → π_1 P_{D'*}.

Purpose. This is gluing data for the 'structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller tower. The fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum (where tangential base points live) is identified with that of the deleted normal bundle. These comparison maps glue the groupoids Π̃_{d_0,…,d_r} attached to strata.

What follows. The page ends with the wish for a more 'canonical' gluing. The next page reverses the arrow, (243) Π_1^ouv P_{D*} → Π̃_1 V^*_{D',Y}, using paths on the source and 1-connected coverings on the target. This avoids needing the tubular embedding and its genericity hypotheses.
errors: No mathematical error. The difficulty he flags is real. For Deligne–Mumford orbifolds (finite stabilizers), averaging an invariant metric gives equivariant smooth tubular neighbourhoods locally; the global stack-theoretic construction, compatibility with the full stratification and holomorphy are the genuine issues.

His counterexample uses Z acting with infinite stabilizers: the transvection fixes the line y=0 pointwise. So it shows failure for general 'multiplicités', not for the finite-stabilizer moduli stacks actually at stake. The text does not make this distinction explicit.

The marginal claim (π_1 equivalence after removing the deeper strata, via non-singular loci) is asserted without proof. It needs a codimension/purity argument; it is plausible, but on this page it is only gestured at.

ideas.what: Identify π_1 of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a boundary divisor with π_1 of the deleted normal bundle over the open stratum, via a retraction V*→P_{D'*}
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / fundamental groupoid at infinity; deleted normal bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); for M_{g,n}: Ihara–Nakamura (1997), Nakamura, Zoonekynd
ideas.where_published: The idea of 'structure à l'infini' and gluing of fundamental groupoids along the boundary is outlined in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific construction is not, to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Failure of tubular neighbourhoods for multiplicities (example: Z acting on C^2 by a transvection gives a non-split normal extension)
ideas.modern_name: Non-existence of equivariant tubular neighbourhoods for non-proper actions / stacks with infinite stabilizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of equivariant differential topology (Palais, Mostow for proper actions)

ideas.what: Two fundamental groupoids for multiplicities: π_1^ouv (points and paths) versus π_1^rev (coverings), and comparing them
ideas.where_published: Possibly La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), which the next page seems to cite as 'Mon p. 779 ff' – unsure

ideas.what: Reversing the comparison arrow (paths on the deleted normal bundle into the covering-defined groupoid of V*) to avoid choosing tubular neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: Canonical specialization / gluing maps of fundamental groupoids along boundary strata

missed.claim: A working record of Grothendieck's technical obstacle to building the Teichmüller tower's gluing data: tubular neighbourhoods may not exist for multiplicities. His fix is a path-to-covering comparison arrow, which anticipates the tangential-base-point formalism later done algebraically by Deligne and Ihara–Nakamura. It is historically interesting but not mathematically new.
missed.quote: Mais le bât blesse, du fait qu'on n'a pas de c[onn]exité sans supposer la [nécessité] d'hypothèses restrictives génériques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had explicitly worked out the topological groupoid gluing at the boundary of M_{g,ν}. This could inform historical attribution of the 'structure at infinity' programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine technical scaffolding: punctured tubular neighbourhood versus deleted normal bundle, and the resulting π_1 comparison. The content is standard, and later developed in the tangential-base-point literature. Its value is mostly historical.
transcription_corrections: 'Mais le but blesse' should read 'Mais là le bât blesse' (idiom: 'here is the rub').
In the diagram the top arrow goes π_1^ouv P_{D'*} → π_1^rev V_{D',Y}, with a vertical isomorphism π_1^ouv P_{D'*} ≅ π_1^rev P_{D'*}; 'NB π_1^ouv V' is a side remark.

The marginal note reads roughly: 'Mais V*_{D'*} ↪ V*_{D'} → P_{D'*} induit une équivalence sur les π_1 de V*_{D'*} et P_{D'*}, au vu de l'équivalence des π_1 des lieux de non-singularité [?] et de leurs revêtements [?]'.
'que nous [?] plongés (240)' is likely 'que les plongements (240) sont tels que'; 'P^{**}_{D'*}' is likely just P_{D'*}.
'la connexité d'hypothèses' on line 3 more likely reads 'la nécessité d'hypothèses restrictives génériques'; the earlier word is uncertain.
